purpose: Check adapter-recorded, single-sink lifecycle histories against idempotency, receipt-binding, response, and fencing invariants.
ordering: Every event has a contiguous zero-based seq. The adapter must emit a normalized causal order: facts referenced by a committed response must be recorded before that response. seq is not a wall-clock timestamp.

scope.idempotency_key_namespace: one sink_identity_digest for the trace and the sink's documented retention interval
scope.fencing: tokens are monotonic and an effect is accepted only under the currently observed token

invariants.name: contiguous-history
invariants.description: Sequence is contiguous, unique, and ordered.

invariants.name: stable-intent
invariants.description: A key cannot be reused for a different request/effect/policy tuple.

invariants.name: single-logical-effect
invariants.description: A key has no more than one distinct committed effect ID.

invariants.name: receipt-effect-binding
invariants.description: Every receipt names an existing effect and matches its intent, sink, and key.

invariants.name: effect-receipt-pairing
invariants.description: Every observed committed effect has a corresponding receipt in the completed trace.

invariants.name: response-truthfulness
invariants.description: Committed responses reference a prior matching receipt; rejected attempts have no effect or receipt.

invariants.name: fencing
invariants.description: The attempt and effect use the active monotonic fencing token.

reporting.liveness: Observations only; no liveness PASS is inferred without a workload-specific completion bound.

explicit_non_claims: Does not execute a real sink or prove the recorder is honest.
Does not prove durability, crash safety, distributed linearizability, cryptographic authenticity, or production qualification.
Does not establish liveness from safety PASS.
Does not model key expiry or namespace pruning; adapter qualification must provide retention-boundary traces separately.
